label: redundant-code-simplify
name: A statement, member, branch, specifier or scope adds nothing the surrounding code or the language does not already give
description: What breaks: readability only. A lambda forwards all arguments to a function with the identical std::function signature (2954613896); a per-element cast where one pointer cast outside the loop suffices (2700506675 'I know this is pedantic'); a second pos_list_devices() call where the local devs exists (3029340601); an else branch that re-assigns the initial values (2789831855 'else clause is redundant'); 'public:' as the first specifier of a struct (3391446464); a memset and braces left from a loop that became a block (2976643305); nshards next to shards.size() (3010846319); device_idx next to dev->idx (2913598312 'Or is there some transient state ...?'). Procedure: for each added statement ask whether removing it changes any observable state; compare added members with fields reachable from sibling members; compare added calls with locals that already hold the value; compare the first access specifier with the keyword default. Severity is always nit or pedantic; he phrases them as questions and accepts pushback.
disposition_reason: No existing check reads for redundancy; 8 rows over 8 PRs; report as nits only.
agent_feasibility: yes: local reading of the hunk and the enclosing function; low cost, low severity.

members.concern: The observer vectors on_save_k/on_save_v are filled with lambdas that only forward every argument to gof_on_save_k/gof_on_save_v; since those free functions match the std::function signature exactly and no other variant exists, Wade asks whether pushing the function directly would be clearer.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a lambda whose body is a single call forwarding all of its parameters, in order, to one named function, into a std::function (or callback) slot whose signature the named function already matches.
detection.procedure: For each added lambda, parse parameters and body; if the body is one call with the same parameter list, look up the callee's declaration (git grep -n 'void CALLEE(' HEAD -- h) and the std::function alias of the slot (kv_save_observer_t at model.hpp:627); if the signatures match, flag the lambda as removable.
detection.question: Does the lambda add anything (capture, conversion, reordering, default) that the direct function name would not provide?

members.quote:
we don't have any other variants for these callbacks now... and the gof_xxx callbacks match the std::function definition exactly. Would it be clearer to just do
```
on_save_k.push_back(tron::hardware::gof_on_save_k);
```
etc, rather than use the lambda?
members.note: Verified at 8e19ea3e62 model.hpp:795-803: lambdas `[](bf16** h, size_t t, size_t nk, size_t l, size_t hs, tron::node_base* n) { tron::hardware::gof_on_save_k(h, t, nk, l, hs, n); }`; kv_save_observer_t declared at model.hpp:627; gof_on_save_k/v declared at h/tron/gof.hpp:85/91. Author: 'fixed in commit 429249ead' = 'Simplify observer registration; document xfer_gof as temporary'; at head model.hpp:795-797 pushes the functions directly. Posted 5 minutes before Wade's text-less APPROVED review at the same commit, so the approval did not wait for the fix.

members.concern: Wade suggests converting the source pointer once (reinterpret_cast to bf16*) and comparing directly, instead of casting each element `(bf16)original[k]` inside the validation loop.

detection.trigger: A loop body applies the same type cast to every element of a pointer or view whose storage already has the target type.
detection.procedure: Find the declared element type of the indexed object (here `vs` is `intermediate_t<...>` = indexed_vector<token_job_id, btensor_t<width>>; btensor_t is the bf16 tensor type, inference from its name and from the bf16 set_v overload at kv_cache.hpp:483). If the storage type equals the cast target, the cast can be one pointer cast outside the loop.
detection.question: Is the element already stored in the target type, so that one pointer cast outside the loop replaces a cast on every iteration?

members.quote: I know this is pedantic... but could we not do `bf16* original - reinterpret_cast<bf16*>(&vs[ix][kv_head * head_size]);` here, and then just use `original` directly below?
members.note: Wade's suggested line has `-` where `=` is meant (typo). The hunk (gh pr diff 1877) declares `auto* original = &vs[ix][kv_head * head_size];` and then loops `bf16 org_bf = (bf16)original[k]; if (float(recovered[k]) != float(org_bf)) ... std::abort();`. No reply from the author; the PR was closed without merge (head 67b616f064 is not in the worktree history). Wade approved in the same minute as the comment. He did not raise the PR body's own statement that the validation 'should go into a unit test somewhere'.

members.concern: A second site in the same function calls pos_list_devices() again and indexes 0; Wade suggests reusing the already computed local `devs` instead of calling the function again.

detection.trigger: Within one function the diff calls the same zero-argument accessor more than once after already storing its result in a local, or repeats an expression whose value a local already holds.
detection.procedure: For each added function body, list zero-argument calls (pos_list_devices(), getenv, size()) and locals assigned from them; flag later calls of the same accessor in the same scope. A one-line suggestion block replacing the call with the local is the remedy.
detection.question: Does a local in the same scope already hold this value, so the repeated call is a second evaluation that can diverge or costs a lookup for nothing?

members.note: No reply from the author. At head 1a88e897e1 full.hpp:1623 still reads `auto dev = (*pos_list_devices())[0];`, so the suggestion was not applied. Same approximate-suggestion issue as 3029339639 (`devs` is a pointer). Wade did not say 'nit'; severity minor is inferred from the suggestion-only form. This is the one comment in the PR that is pure style/duplication, with no behavior question.

members.concern: After 'readback_addr = nullptr; readback_value = 0;' the if/else sets the same values again in the else branch, so the else clause is dead repetition.

detection.trigger: An added if/else where the else branch assigns variables to the same values they were initialised with a few lines above, or an added 'x = x' style no-op.
detection.procedure: For each added else branch, list its assignments and compare each right-hand side with the initializer of the same variable in the lines above the if. If every assignment equals the initializer, the branch is redundant. Verify by reading the function at HEAD.
detection.question: Does the else branch change any state that the initialisation above it did not already set?

members.quote: `else` clause is redundant... already initialized to these values to begin with
members.note: At head d4795f37a5 driver.cpp lines 795-802 keep the initialisers and the if, with no else; the function returns '{q, final_desc, wrap_count, readback_addr, readback_value}'. Author: 'was trying to be explicit', removed.

members.concern: The new struct inflight_guard (an RAII credit holder) starts with an explicit 'public:' access specifier, which is the default for a struct and so redundant.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a 'struct X {' followed by 'public:' as the first access specifier, or a 'class X {' followed by 'private:' as the first specifier.
detection.procedure: grep -n -A1 '^struct .*{$' over the added lines and flag a following 'public:'; grep -n -A1 '^class .*{$' and flag a following 'private:'. Check that no earlier non-default specifier precedes it inside the same type.
detection.question: Is the first access specifier in this type the same as the keyword's default?

members.quote: minor nit: `public` is redundant in a struct (members are public by default)
members.note: At ffc2d6156a h/tron/gof.hpp:117-118: 'struct inflight_guard {' then 'public:'. Author fixed it in commit 'Remove redundant public specifier in inflight_guard' (reply 2026-06-11). This contradicts the skill's current sentence 'He does not comment on formatting, brace style': he does post language-hygiene nits on redundant keywords. Posted 11 minutes before his APPROVED review, so it did not block.

members.concern: Wade notes that the test's per-device loop became a single block, so the memset that reset `dest` between iterations is no longer needed, and the leftover enclosing braces and indentation can go.

detection.trigger: A diff turns a `for` or `while` header into a bare `{` block (or deletes the loop) while keeping the loop body unchanged.
detection.procedure: Read the whole block at HEAD, not only the hunk the comment lands on (the loop-to-block change is a different hunk, t_mwaitx.cpp:223-226 in the PR diff; the memset is at :273). List statements in the body that only make sense across iterations: resets at the end of the body (memset, clear, counter reset), per-iteration re-initialisation. Flag them plus the now-pointless scope.
detection.question: With the loop gone, does any statement in the former body exist only to prepare the next iteration?

members.quote: a bit pedantic but you're no longer running a loop, so this isn't necessary... and perhaps get rid of the extra scope (remove enclosing curly brackets, un-indent this block)
members.note: Read at commit 83ab846277 (t_mwaitx.cpp:226-263): the block starts with `{ auto dev = all_devs.front();` (was `for (auto dev : *pos_list_devices())`) and ends with `memset(dest, 0, test_size); cycle_stat_elapsed(...); }`. Wade approved one minute later at the same commit. At the worktree HEAD the file still has the memset at line 273 and the block, so the nit was not applied; no author reply in the digest.

members.concern: He asks whether `nshards` is ever different from `shards.size()` and, if not, whether the separate count is redundant.

detection.trigger: A diff adds a container member and a separate count member side by side.
detection.procedure: Read the container's declared type: for std::vector the count is redundant; for std::array<T, N> or T[N] `.size()` is the fixed capacity N, so the count is needed (fill level). Then grep all writers of the count.
detection.question: Is the container's size() the fill level or the fixed capacity?

members.quote: is there ever an expected scenario where `nshards` != `shards.size()`? If not it seems like `nshards` is redundant since you can always use shards.size()
members.note: The member is `std::array<shard_layer_t, MAX_B> shards{}` (device.hpp:93 at head), so shards.size() is always 32 and nshards is the fill count; the question rests on a misread of std::array as std::vector. No reply in the digest; PR merged the same day. Shows Wade asks a question when unsure rather than asserting, and that his questions can be wrong on the C++ fact.

members.concern: struct shard (metadata for a 1024-token HBM region on one FPGA) stores both a uint32_t device_idx and a PosDevice* dev pointer; Wade asks whether device_idx is redundant with dev->idx, or whether there is a transient state with a valid index but a null device pointer that justifies keeping both.

detection.trigger: A diff adds a struct with two members where one (an index, id or size) can be read from another member (a pointer to an object that carries the same field).
detection.procedure: For each new struct, list members that are ids or indices. For each, check whether a sibling pointer member's type exposes the same value (grep the pointee type for `idx`). Then grep every writer of the id member; if every writer also sets the pointer, or a writer leaves the pointer null while setting the id, decide. Phrase the finding as a question with the 'transient state' alternative.
detection.question: Is there any lifetime window where the index is valid but the pointer is null, so that the index cannot be replaced by pointer->idx?

members.quote: isn't `device_idx` redundant here? We can always get that from `PosDevice->idx`. Or is there some transient state where we expect to have a valid 'device_idx' but a NULL 'dev'?
members.note: Verified at dbd7478b7e: struct shard had `uint32_t device_idx = 0;  // which FPGA` and `PosDevice* dev = nullptr;` on consecutive lines [h/pos/gof.hpp at dbd7478b7e]. Commit 3b8314a1 ('remove redundant device_idx from shard') dropped the field from h/tron/shard.hpp (the header had been moved by then) and changed src/tron/gof.cpp to use `sh->dev->idx`. Wade knew PosDevice has an idx member (knowledge of h/pos types, not in the hunk). Question form with two alternatives, matching the skill's 'design concern is a question with two alternatives' rule.
